Chapter 6: Mastering Leverage—People, Processes, and Partnerships
Now that you’ve built a strong foundation and put systems in place, it’s time to talk about something that can truly multiply your impact—leverage.
When I say leverage, I’m talking about using resources like people, processes, and partnerships to get results that go way beyond what you could ever do on your own.
Think of it like pushing a huge boulder uphill. Doing it alone is tough, right? But if you have the right lever, suddenly, moving that boulder feels a whole lot easier.
The first kind of leverage is people. As your business grows, it’s just not possible—or healthy—to try to do everything yourself.
Building a team, whether it’s employees, contractors, or collaborators, lets you focus on what you do best, while others handle the pieces they’re great at.
But here’s something to really pay attention to: don’t just hire for skills. Look for people who actually believe in your business’s values and vision.
When your team feels connected to your purpose, they’re more likely to go the extra mile—sometimes doing way more than their job description asks.
Now, let’s talk about processes. We touched on this earlier, but as you bring people on board, well-documented workflows become even more powerful.
With clear systems, new team members can get up to speed fast, and your business runs smoothly—even as it grows.
At this point, things start to click; your business feels less like a random pile of tasks and more like a living, breathing organism, with every part working together.
Partnerships are another layer of leverage that’s easy to overlook.
By teaming up with other businesses, influencers, or organizations, you can tap into new markets, skills, and resources.
The best partnerships aren’t just about a quick win—they’re built on real alignment and shared values.
For example, imagine a service-based business partnering with a company that offers a related solution. Together, they can create bundled packages, helping both businesses reach more people.
So, how do you actually put leverage into practice? Here are a few steps you can use right away:
First—figure out your core strengths, then delegate or outsource everything else.
Next, create onboarding and training materials, so any new team member feels empowered from day one.
And finally, look for partnerships that truly align with your mission and can help you expand your reach.
Picture this: a business owner who’s been doing everything alone finally hires a project manager and forms a joint venture with a trusted peer.
Suddenly, the business starts to grow faster and with less stress. The owner has more time to focus on big ideas and innovation, instead of being stuck in the daily grind.
So here’s the key takeaway: leverage isn’t about giving up control. It’s about multiplying what you’re capable of—honoring your mission, taking care of your well-being, and making sure your growth is both sustainable and truly rewarding.
